I fixed the one verified finding — the FIG. 1 / FIG. 4 fence geometry conflict — by conforming the figure briefs (and the FIG. 4 drawing description that names its view type) to the longitudinal-side relationship the inventor disclosed. No claim, numeral, or embodiment text was narrowed to accommodate a drawing.

**What was wrong:** FIG. 4 fixed a geometry in which the workpiece edge 92 was the panel's left-hand *end* face with the rail running perpendicular to it, putting the downwardly projecting portion 32 beyond the rail's first end rather than on a longitudinal side — mutually exclusive with FIG. 6, the reversible-fence paragraph, and claims 1, 16 and 20, where inverting the fence moves that portion from one longitudinal side to the opposite one. FIG. 1 carried the same arrangement in weaker form.

**What I changed:** FIG. 4 is now an elevation taken looking along the rail's length, with the rail seen end-on set inward from the edge, the fence crossing it transversely and reaching toward the edge, and portion 32 standing on the longitudinal side of the rail that faces edge 92, with spacer plate 40 between them. FIG. 1 now shows the rail spaced inward from and parallel to edge 92, with portion 32 on the rail's edge-facing longitudinal side. `draft/07-drawings.md` was updated to match FIG. 4's new view type, and one clause in the detailed description now states the longitudinal-side position where the fence is first introduced, so the relationship is unambiguous at every mention. The numeral table needed no change; every numeral in both briefs is still used.

One note on the record, per the drafting brief: no prior-art search was run for this application, so the art in `prior_art/` may be incomplete.
